rows.detail: double single: the larger of 1e-13 of F_n(x) and 1e-13 of F_0(x) - the accuracy contract's figure over the whole domain, the ladder's first rung being its wider arm wherever the order's own value is the smaller - which is what the four regions the report reads are each judged against. The figure is the shipped default build's: a build whose default rows are a replacement's records these cells and
double batch: the larger of 1e-13 of F_n(x) and 1e-13 of F_0(x) in every region, all entries. The figure is the shipped default build's, on the same terms as the row above
float single and batch: 2^-22 of F_n(x), or its 1.5e-7 floor where that is the larger, in every region, and 1e-7 beside it in the plain-reciprocal form - the lane's own bar, not 1e-13 scaled

domain: the arguments where |F_n(x)| > 1e-7 + one half-ULP of the returned value, and no others - the restriction the half lanes' paragraph in docs/lane-contract.md states. The row judges at that base, which is the region target the half lanes' fits are cut for and is tighter than the 1.5e-7 the library publishes for them, so its domain is wider than the published claim's and a pass here is the st

double single: the larger of 1e-13 of F_n(x) and 1e-13 of F_0(x) in the region-A and extended-band cells the header's table keeps apart. The figure is the shipped default build's, on the same terms as README.double.single

the stored coefficients are rounded to double precision and hold only the sixteen or so significant digits a double can hold, so nothing below about 1e-16 is reachable however the evaluation is arranged - the fit's own truncation, 5e-19, sits under that floor and is not a second bound

the ceiling is the format: a 32-bit float carries about seven significant digits, about 6e-8 relative, and the lane's relative arm is 4.0 times that digit (2^-22 / 6e-8), so the two are within a factor of a few of each other; at F_n(x) = 1e-3 the relative arm is 2.4e-10, far below the 1.5e-7 the lane can hold there, and the plain-reciprocal form adds its 1e-7 term to the larger of the two

domain: region A - both bands, x < kRegionA1Edge and kRegionA1Edge <= x < kRegionAEnd - every order 0..32, every argument of the band. domain: the arguments where |F_n(x)| > 1e-7 + one half-ULP of the returned value, and no others - the base the half lanes' fits are cut for, tighter than the 1.5e-7 the library publishes for them

both formats' worst cells were measured against a 45-digit reference over every argument either format can represent and every order - a 16-bit input is a finite set, so that sweep is exhaustive rather than dense: 0.9993 of the bound for the 16-bit format, a margin of 0.07 per cent, and 0.99992 for the 16-bit brain-float format, a margin of 0.008 per cent; a sparser grid understates them, the comm
at the worst cell the representation term is very nearly the whole bound, and the arithmetic term has almost nothing left to spend

domain: the arguments where |F_n(x)| > 1e-7 + one half-ULP of the returned value - the domain a base the half lanes' fits are cut for carves, tighter than the 1.5e-7 the library publishes and so wider than the published claim, and no others
domain: orders 3 to 32 on region C (x >= kX1), the part of the half lane's argument range where the returns are subnormal or zero
beyond about x ~ 35-38 no scaling reaches order 8 at all
a per-order power-of-two rescale does not repair the packed lane because the rescale is exact, leaving the scaled lane bit-identical to the unscaled one at every order
the 8-wide half-I/O region kernels never drift from the certified scalar half lane by a value the internal 1e-7 fit budgets cannot absorb, on the x86_64 targets that carry those kernels
the 8-wide half-I/O region kernels hold the published half-lane budget (1.5e-7 plus one half-ULP) on the region each documents as its precondition

the fp16/bf16 budget is a claim only where the returned value exceeds it: below that ceiling the format's floor answers and no accuracy is claimed; in f16 the ceiling and the floor coincide, so every argument past it returns a subnormal half and then exactly zero, while in bf16 the exponent range equals float's, so the base is met by the arithmetic down to about 2^-126
domain: region C, x >= 28.984375 = fp16(kX1), over the arguments whose returned value is a normal half - the lane offers no other region and claims no accuracy outside it
domain: region C, x >= 28.984375 = fp16(kX1), where the ceiling is what the lane's own scaling reaches
domain: region C, x >= 28.984375 = fp16(kX1), the only region the lane evaluates in
domain: region C, x >= fp16(kX1) = 28.984375, and only there
[corrected this revision] region B's amplification is one plus 1.8e-17 at order 32 - above one, not at most one - and that is its maximum over the supported orders
[corrected this revision] rounding the coefficients to double contributes about 5.551e-17 - the half-ULP of the leading coefficient alone - and not 3e-17

no lane's claim is unchecked at the top of its own argument range: the sweep reaches binary16's largest finite value for the half lanes and binary32's for the floats, and nothing above binary32's maximum is a range any lane of this library evaluates in

[corrected this revision] the branch's lower boundary is not a floor: through x = 16 the error varies smoothly, with no threshold and no step of orders of magnitude, growing continuously as x falls below the edge
the documented budgets are re-checkable with ctest
